title: In 64 Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels mice, the change response predicted hits equally weakly from LGd to higher visual cortex after state control; only midbrain units added information beyond V1
abstract: We tested where along the anatomical pathway the image-change response predicts whether a mouse detects the change (hit) or misses it. We used 78 Familiar sessions of Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels; 64 mice had enough engaged trials (6,654 hits, 2,248 misses; 21,858 units). Unit detect probability (DP, hit versus miss AUROC, 20-150 ms after change, before licks) was very small. The raw DP increased with the Harris 2019 hierarchy score (slope +0.011 per score unit [+0.005, +0.019]), but the pre-change flash, which has no change information, had almost the same slope (+0.009). After regression of running, pupil, trial time and reward rate, change DP was +0.011 to +0.015 in every thalamocortical area, including LGd (+0.014 [+0.006, +0.024]); the slope was +0.002 [-0.003, +0.008] and pre-change DP was near zero. The change signal itself was 2 to 8 times larger and about 13-22% weaker on misses in thalamocortical areas, but 37-61% weaker in superior colliculus and MRN. Behaviour alone decoded hits with AUROC 0.62; 15 units of any thalamocortical area added at most 0.011 beyond V1 and behaviour, while SCm, MRN and APN units added 0.03-0.05. Thus the hierarchy did not amplify the change-specific hit/miss signal; an uncontrolled state confound produces a false gradient. Limitations: correlational, measured covariates only, small effects, 15-unit decoders, Familiar sessions only.

(A) Raw hit/miss detect probability by area. (B) The change signal (change versus pre-change flash) and the hit/miss signal on the same AUROC scale.
(A) Cross-validated hit/miss decoding from 15 units per area, behaviour alone (grey band) and behaviour plus units. (B) Gain of a second area over 15 V1 units plus behaviour.
